name: Ullu
tagline: Every night the owl brings fortune. The light decides where.
description: Ullu is the owl who brings fortune to the brightest house on the street. Every visitor gets a house, lights it night after night and decorates it with what the owl leaves. Seven nights in a row and the owl lands on your roof with a sack of gold.

hero.text: In India they say the owl carries fortune, and it flies to the brightest light. So every night the whole street lights up, and every house hopes the owl lands on its roof. Here you get a house of your own. Light it up.

hero.alt: Ullu, a fat owl in a saffron turban, sits on gold coins with a cup of chai and winks
hero.note: He does not knock. He looks for the light.

lore.title: The owl goes where the light is brightest
lore.lead: Ullu means owl. In Hindi it also means a fool. He is both, and he is never wrong about money.

cards.title: He flies at night
cards.text: Every night Ullu flies over the city with a sack of fortune. He does not read names on doors. He looks for the brightest window.

cards.title: So everyone lights up
cards.text: Lamps on the sills, lights on the roofs, flowers on the doors. Every house wants to be the one the owl sees first.

cards.title: Seven nights in a row
cards.text: Light your house every night. On the seventh night in a row the owl lands on your roof, puts on his sunglasses and leaves the whole sack.

rules: On your first visit the street builds you a house. It is yours: nobody else has the same one.
Once a night, press Light up. The owl flies by and leaves something: a lamp, lights, flowers, sometimes one slipper.
Hang what he left on your house. Every night the house is brighter and the owl comes closer.
Miss a night and the house goes dark. The run starts again from night one.
Night seven: the owl lands on your roof with a sack of gold. Save the card, share it, put the house on the street.

rules.title: What the street does and does not do

items.title: Your house lives in your browser
items.text: There is no login and no wallet connection. The site remembers your house in this browser. Clear the browser data and the house is gone. To move it to another phone, copy the house code.

items.title: Where you are stays with you
items.text: On your first visit the site asks the server which city you are near, only to suggest a street and to write the city on your cards. The server does not keep it. The city stays in your browser and never goes to the street.

items.title: The owl is a game
items.text: The gifts, the nights and the sack of gold are pictures on this site. They are not tokens, not rewards and not a promise of anything.

items.title: Your own sign is public
items.text: If your house stands on the street, the words on your own neon sign are seen by everyone. Latin letters and numbers only, no links. Signs that break the rules are taken down.

items.title: The street shows what you send
items.text: Only the house, its name and its nights go to the street. The server draws the house from its code and counts its light itself. There is no proof of the nights: it is a game, not a leaderboard of money.

items.title: The holder preview is a preview
items.text: The switch shows what holders could get: golden lights and clean cards. It does not check any wallet. Golden lights never go to the street.

items.title: Your pictures stay with you
items.text: The picture tool works inside your browser. Nothing you upload leaves your phone.

nights: Night one. The street is dark and quiet. One lamp in your window. Somewhere above, wings.
Night two. A stray cat moved onto your doorstep. Cats always know where the warm light is.
Night three. A chai cart parked next to your house. The street is starting to gather.
Night four. The neighbours hung lights of their own. It is a competition now.
Night five. Fireworks far away. A kid with a sparkler runs past your door.
Night six. Faces in every window. The whole street is watching the sky. So is the owl.
Night seven. The street goes quiet. The owl lands on your roof, puts on his sunglasses and opens the sack.
after: Night {n}. The owl lives here now. He has opinions about your curtains.
Night {n}. The owl invited his cousins. They are sitting on the wires.
Night {n}. The street calls your house 'the owl house' now.
Night {n}. The owl says the sack is getting lighter. He is lying.
Night {n}. Your house is on the owl's map now. Marked in gold.
Night {n}. The cat and the owl have agreed to share the roof. For now.

events.diwali: Festival of lights! The whole country is glowing tonight and the owl is working overtime. He left three gifts instead of one.
events.holi: Holi! Somebody threw colour powder at your house. It is pink now. Partly green. The owl brought marigolds and a rangoli to match.
events.lunar: Lunar New Year! Red lanterns on every door, fireworks on every roof. The owl brought two lanterns for yours.
events.newyear: New Year's night. Fireworks everywhere. The owl brought extra fairy lights and asked for a raise.
events.fullmoon: Full moon. The owl can see every roof in the city tonight, and he still picked yours. Double gift.
events.newmoon: No moon tonight. Your house is the only light on the street. The owl came straight to you and left an extra lamp.
events.latenight: It is {time}. Only you and the owl are awake. He left an extra feather for keeping him company.
events.early: You lit up before it was even dark. The owl saw it from three streets away.
events.weekend: Weekend night. The street is having a party and your house is the dance floor.
events.neighbour: {friend} next door waved from the window. Two lit houses side by side: the owl noticed.
events.powercut: Power cut on the whole street! Every window went dark except yours. Guess which house the owl saw first.
events.rain: It rained all evening. Your lamps hissed but held on. The owl hates wet feathers and came anyway.
events.monsoon: Monsoon rain. The street is a river, the chai cart is a boat, and your lights are the lighthouse.
events.fog: Thick fog tonight. You could not see the house across the street. The owl found you by the glow alone.
events.wedding: A wedding procession danced past with a brass band. Somebody threw marigolds on your doorstep.
events.kite: A runaway kite got stuck on your roof. The owl says it is a sign. Of what, he would not say.
events.skylanterns: The whole street let paper lanterns into the sky. One came back down on your roof.
events.shootingstar: A shooting star fell right behind your roof. The owl says he did that. He left a feather as proof.
events.rickshaw: An auto-rickshaw stopped at your door, honked twice and drove away. Nobody knows why. The owl is suspicious.
events.monkey: A monkey climbed onto your roof and borrowed your {loan}. He promised to bring it back on your next night.
events.goat: A goat walked in, stared at your lights for a long time and walked out. A tough critic.
events.cricket: Big cricket match tonight. Half the street is watching TV. The other half is watching your house.
events.market: A night market popped up in front of your house. Everyone is shopping under your lights.
events.bats: Bats flew over the street at dusk. The owl told them to move along. This is his route.
events.jealous: The neighbours bought more lights. The aunty next door says your house is 'a bit much'. Keep going.
events.counting: A kid on the next roof is counting your lights instead of stars. He got to {count} and started again.
events.owllate: The owl was late tonight. He blames traffic. Owls do not have traffic.
events.selfie: The owl took a selfie with your house. It is his lock screen now.
events.wronghouse: The owl flew to the wrong house first. Then he saw your lights and turned around.
events.chaiflood: The chai seller ran out of cups and served chai in your flower pots. Business is booming.
events.tourists: Tourists stopped to take photos of your house. You are a landmark now.
events.sandstorm: A small sandstorm swept the street. Your lights shone through the dust like gold.
events.scooters: A hundred scooters drove past your house tonight. Every single one slowed down to look.
events.camel: A camel stopped in front of your house and refused to move. He likes the lights too.
events.quiet: A quiet night. Just you, your lights and the owl somewhere above.
events.society: A notice from the housing society: 'Too many lights on floor three.' The owl ate the notice.
events.carrom: The neighbours played carrom under your lights until 2 a.m. They say your house brings luck.
events.tram: The night tram rang its bell twice as it passed your house. The owl rang back.
events.adda: The neighbours held an adda on your steps till midnight. Topic of the night: your lights.
events.fishermen: Fishermen coming back from the sea stopped to look at your lights. One of them said it is brighter than the lighthouse.

howToBuy.title: Get a wallet
howToBuy.text: Install Phantom or Solflare from the official website or app store. Show your seed phrase to no one. Not even the owl.

howToBuy.title: Get some SOL
howToBuy.text: Buy SOL on an exchange or in the wallet and send it to your address. Keep a little for fees.

howToBuy.title: Open guru.fun
howToBuy.text: Go to guru.fun and find $ULLU by the contract address on this page. No address here means no token yet.

howToBuy.title: Swap SOL for $ULLU
howToBuy.text: Choose the amount and confirm in your wallet. Only use money you can afford to lose. The owl does not cover losses.
